summary: Nightly background-batch spike causing dedicated pool throughput collapse
description: Issue summary: During the customer's scheduled nightly batch window (03:00-04:30 UTC) their dedicated pool experienced a rapid p99 latency and throughput collapse across multiple routes. Impact: customer reports ~80% failed requests (429/5xx) for user-facing routes and severe degradation of batch job completion times. This is affecting production inference for payment-risk scoring and is causing customer alerts to fire. Environment: Dedicated pool (Finova-dedicated-us-east), prod, serving-runtime v1.24, scheduler v3.8.
steps_to_reproduce: Observe traffic pattern: small concurrent background batch jobs (20-40 concurrent short streams, median 600ms) scheduled every minute during 03:00-04:30 UTC
Run synthetic load: replay a mix of 500 short streaming requests + 50 long generation requests pinned to same pool
Monitor autoscaler and GPU allocation during burst window
logs: [2026-03-12T03:07:15Z] runtime: batch_serialize start size=38 tenant=finova route=/v1/generate
[2026-03-12T03:07:22Z] gateway: upstream 502 from runtime instance i-0a1b2c
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: sudden wave of short-duration streams caused slot serialization and prevented larger long-running requests from forming efficient batches, amplifying per-token overhead.
Autoscaler behavior: rapid scale-up triggered by CPU heuristic, but stabilization window (30s) too short given high churn of short streams -> oscillation and fragmented GPU allocation.
Observed high eviction counts and slot preemption logs coinciding with the batch window; GPU allocation logs show many small allocations rather than steady larger allocations.

Customer-side discovery: Finova scheduled a new background job (payment-postprocess) that submits many short inference streams without any jitter/backoff; start time changed last week to the same nightly window.
Related signals: console dashboards show prefix cache misses increased 4x during window, KV cache warmed less effectively due to short-lived streams.
Cross refs: Slack thread #support-dedicated (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C05XYZ) contains sample traces; relacionado PR to scheduler for allocation smoothing exists (PR 7123).

Temporary mitigation applied: moved customer to an isolated reserved pool (finova-iso-us-east) and adjusted autoscaler min_replicas from 8 -> 12 and stabilization window -> 120s to reduce oscillation.
resolution: Workaround deployed: customer isolated to temporary reserved pool and autoscaler policy tuned to increase min_replicas and stabilization window. Root causes are (1) high-frequency short streams from customer's background job causing slot serialization and cache churn; (2) autoscaler stabilization too aggressive leading to oscillation and allocation fragmentation. Next steps: schedule follow-up with Finova to throttle and jitter background job, patch scheduler to implement small-stream aggregation and per-tenant short-stream smoothing (plan PR underway: github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/7123), and add runtime metric alarms for short-stream churn. Will monitor through next 72h.
